title: Keep useful context between sessions
problem: My agent loses the thread when I start a new session.
summary: Make a small handoff, check its source, then reuse it in the next session.
evidence: Architecture account: explains the design and its limits; it does not measure a recall improvement.

steps.title: Capture one decision
steps.body: Use a repository you know. Replace the example's file and heading with a real source. Keep the uncertainty line until you have checked the command.
steps.code:
# Session handoff
Goal: document how this repository starts locally.
Decision: start with README.md, section Development.
Evidence: README.md, section Development.
Uncertainty: the startup command has not been run here.
Next step: read the prerequisites, then test the documented command.
Constraint: do not change application code.

steps.title: Ask a bounded question
steps.body: Give your agent the handoff and the source section. If it cannot read files, paste that section with its file name and heading.
steps.code:
Read the handoff and README.md, section Development.
List the exact prerequisites and startup command.
Cite the file and heading for each answer.
Say what the source does not establish.
Do not run commands or change files.

steps.title: Check and carry it forward
steps.body: Open every cited heading. Correct invented prerequisites. Record an observed result only after running the command in the stated environment. Give the next session the short handoff; retain the detailed log separately.

check: The next session can name the goal, the source, what remains untested and one next action.

title: Give an agent the context the task needs
problem: My agent gets too much context, or misses the evidence that matters.
summary: Choose one reference, set a source boundary and check the answer against it.
evidence: Controlled experiment: 256 runs, two small repositories and one model. Files on disk alone did not establish savings; the result does not generalize to every agent or task.

steps.title: Start with one question
steps.body: Write the question before collecting files. This example asks for documented cache conditions, not general advice.
steps.code:
Question: What conditions must a prompt satisfy to be cached?
Need: documented conditions, exceptions and source links.
Exclude: unrelated model comparisons and performance guesses.

steps.title: Choose and supply one reference
steps.body: Open Prompt caching in the research library. Check the sources and their dates. Download its facts file if your agent cannot open links. Attach only the relevant facets.
steps.code:
Read the supplied reference before answering.
For each caching condition, cite the original source.
Distinguish the documented condition from your inference.
If a source date or model boundary is missing, say so.
Do not turn an example into a universal guarantee.

steps.title: Verify the answer and reduce the handoff
steps.body: Follow two of the source links and compare the actual passage with the answer. Keep the useful conditions and their source pointers. Remove context that did not help answer the question.

check: Each retained claim has a source you can open, and the answer states its model/version limits.

title: Maintain a skill you can test
problem: My installed skills are hard to trust or maintain.
summary: Review one instruction, compare a small task set and keep a reversible change.
evidence: Technical paper: explains how the optimizer family, including skill-optimizer, audits and revises a skill. It reports no measured result for the illustrative notes skill below.

steps.title: Save the current instruction
steps.body: Choose one skill and keep a backup. For a small local exercise, use the intentionally underspecified instruction below.
steps.code: Summarize these notes and tell me what to do next.

steps.title: Review one concrete weakness
steps.body: The instruction does not say how to treat missing dates or conflicting statements. The revision below adds an explicit output and source boundary. This is an instruction review, not evidence of improved model performance.
steps.code:
Summarize only the supplied numbered notes.
Return: Decision, Evidence, Uncertainty, Next step.
Cite the note number for each factual statement.
If a date or owner is absent, write Unknown.
Preserve conflicting statements with both note numbers.
Do not invent a deadline, owner or completed action.

steps.title: Run a small before/after task set
steps.body: Use the same model, settings and source notes for both versions. Run each case in a fresh session. Record the exact model/version, results, token usage and cost if your runner exposes them. Keep missing telemetry as unavailable.
steps.code:
Case A: [1] Use the documented startup command. [2] It has not been tested here.
Check: does the answer keep the command untested?

Case B: [1] Review the setup guide.
Check: are owner and deadline Unknown?

Case C: [1] Release date is Monday. [2] Release date is Tuesday.
Check: does the answer preserve both dates and cite both notes?

Score each case: 1 only if the answer passes its check and every fact cites a supplied note; otherwise 0.
Record each answer and total /3 for both instructions.
These three cases demonstrate the evaluation method; they do not establish general quality.

steps.title: Adopt or restore
steps.body: Keep the revision only if it improves the task you care about without breaking another case. Record the failure if it does not. Read the optimizer's full prompt and requirements before using it on a real library. Skills Explorer helps inspect the installed files and saved evaluation results.

check: You have the two instructions, six saved answers, the /3 scores, the model/settings and a reason to keep or restore the change. No model run or performance gain is claimed by this example.
